Note that the non-emptiness of  $ \widehat{C}_1(t) $ depends on the size of the tightening terms  $ \epsilon $,  $ \epsilon_b $, which are largest at  $ t = 0 $ and shrink as the certified bounds  $ \rho_i(t) $ decrease. In practice,  $ \widehat{C}_1(t) $ can be made non-empty by choosing a sufficiently short backup horizon  $ T $ or a sufficiently tight initial parameter box  $ \Theta $, and becomes progressively less conservative as the estimator refines the parameter estimate. To ensure robust safety in the case of potential infeasibility of the QP, the robust backup controller  $ k_b $ can be utilized. By Assumption 2,  $ k_b $ renders  $ C_1 $ forward invariant along (10), and satisfies  $ \mathbf{k}_b(\boldsymbol{x}) \in \mathcal{U} $ for all  $ \boldsymbol{x} \in C_1 $. Therefore, if (35) becomes infeasible, one can switch to  $ k_b $ to keep the state in  $ \mathcal{C}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{C}_S $ while satisfying the input constraints. A smooth switching between  $ k^* $ and  $ k_b $ can also be used, as in [19].
### V. PLANAR QUADROTOR EXAMPLE

We illustrate the proposed control method using a planar quadrotor example with parametric uncertainty in both the drift and input matrices†. The state and input vectors are  $ \boldsymbol{x} \triangleq [p_x \quad p_z \quad \vartheta \quad v_x \quad v_z \quad \omega]^\top \in \mathcal{X} $,  $ \boldsymbol{u} \triangleq [F \quad M]^\top \in \mathcal{U} $, where  $ \mathcal{X} \subset \mathbb{R}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1 \times \mathbb{R}^3 $,  $ p_x $ and  $ p_z $ denote the horizontal and vertical quadrotor positions,  $ \vartheta $ is its pitch angle, and  $ (v_x, v_z, \omega) $ are the translational and angular velocities. The inputs are the thrust force  $ F $ and pitch moment  $ M $, with  $ \mathcal{U} \triangleq [0, F_{\max}] \times [-M_{\max}, M_{\max}] \subset \mathbb{R}^2 $. The planar quadrotor model is

$$ \begin{align*}\dot{p}_{x}&=v_{x},\quad\dot{p}_{z}=v_{z},\quad\vartheta=\omega,\quad\dot{\omega}=\delta_{\ell}F-\frac{1}{J}M,\\\dot{v}_{x}&=-c_{x}v_{x}+\frac{\sin\vartheta}{m}F,\quad\dot{v}_{z}=-c_{z}v_{z}-g+\frac{\cos\vartheta}{m}F,\end{align*} $$

where  $ c_x $ and  $ c_z $ are damping coefficients,  $ g $ is the gravitational acceleration,  $ m $ is the mass of the quadrotor,  $ J $ is its mass moment of inertia, and  $ \delta_\ell $ captures an unknown pitch moment generated by thrust. We assume that each of these six parameters is uncertain, and the nominal values used for control design are  $ 0 $,  $ 0 $,  $ g_0 $,  $ m_0 $,  $ J_0 $, and  $ 0 $, respectively.

Accordingly, we introduce the unknown parameter vector  $ \boldsymbol{\theta} \triangleq [c_x \quad c_z \quad \delta_g \quad \delta_m \quad \delta_J \quad \delta_\ell]^\top \in \Theta \subset \mathbb{R}^6 $, with  $ \delta_g \triangleq g - g_0 $,  $ \delta_m \triangleq \frac{1}{m} - \frac{1}{m_0} $,  $ \delta_J \triangleq \frac{1}{J} - \frac{1}{J_0} $, and we separate the nominal model and the uncertainty as

We remark that  $ c_x $,  $ c_z $, and  $ \delta_g $ introduce drift uncertainty, while the uncertainties  $ \delta_m $,  $ \delta_J $, and  $ \delta_\ell $ enter through the actuation matrix and multiply the control input, which is addressed by the duality-based robustification in Section IV. Note that the regression matrix  $ \phi(x,u) $ is affine in  $ u $.

The insertion task is executed by a primary controller  $ k_p $ that is a cascaded position-attitude law steering the quadrotor to a goal  $ (p_x^g, p_z^g) $:  $ a_x = -k_p^x(p_x + p_z^g) - k_d^x v_x $,  $ a_z = -k_p^z(p_z - p_z^g) - k_d^z v_z $,  $ F = m_0 \sqrt{a_x^2 + (g_0 + a_z)^2} $,  $ \vartheta_d = \text{atan2}(a_x, g_0 + a_z) $,  $ M = J_0 (k_p^y (\vartheta - \vartheta_d) + k_d^y \omega) $, saturated to  $ \mathcal{U} $. Since  $ k_p $ is agnostic to both the safety constraint and the parametric uncertainty, we apply the proposed QP-based safety filter in (35): the DREM estimator of Example 1 provides the parameter estimate  $ \hat{\theta}(t) $ and the certified error bounds  $ \rho_i(t) $, the backup flow is propagated with  $ \hat{\theta}(t) $, and the safety conditions tightened by  $ \rho_i(t) $ are enforced along this flow.
The robust backup controller takes the form

$$ \begin{array}{r l}{\boldsymbol{k}_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})=\left[\boldsymbol{F}_{\mathrm{m a x}}\right.}&{{}\mathrm{s a t}\left(k_{\vartheta}(\vartheta-\vartheta_{\mathrm{r}})+k_{\omega}\omega\right)\right]^{\top},}\end{array} $$

where  $ k_{\vartheta} > 0 $ and  $ k_{\omega} > 0 $ are gains,  $ \vartheta_{\mathrm{r}} \in (0, \vartheta_{\mathrm{max}}) $ is a reference pitch angle, and sat is a smooth saturation map into  $ [-M_{\mathrm{max}}, M_{\mathrm{max}}] $. The corresponding backup set is

$$ \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{B}}\triangleq\left\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathcal{X}\colon\begin{aligned}&h_{x,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})\geq0,\ h_{z,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})\geq0,\ h_{\vartheta,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})\geq0\\ &h_{v_{x},\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})\geq0,\ h_{v_{z},\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})\geq0\end{aligned}\right\}, $$

where  $ h_{x,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = p_x - p_x^{\min} - r_x $ and  $ h_{z,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = p_z - p_z^{\min} - r_z $ represent surface and altitude clearance with margins  $ r_x > 0 $ and  $ r_z > 0 $, while  $ h_{v_x,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = v_x $ and  $ h_{v_z,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = v_z $ prescribe positive velocities. For the pitch dynamics, we let  $ \boldsymbol{y}_\theta \triangleq [\vartheta - \vartheta_\mathrm{r} \, \omega]^\top $ and  $ h_{\vartheta,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = \varrho_\vartheta - \boldsymbol{y}_\vartheta^\top \boldsymbol{P}_\vartheta \boldsymbol{y}_\vartheta $, with  $ \varrho_\vartheta > 0 $ and  $ \boldsymbol{P}_\vartheta = \boldsymbol{P}_\vartheta^\top \gamma > 0 $.
